name: sylvester
expr: X = sylvester(A, B, C); err = max(max(abs(A*X + X*B - C))); Xs = sylvester(single(A), B, C); Xns = sylvester([1 2; 3 5], [1 2; 3 4], C); Xz = sylvester(zeros(2), zeros(2), zeros(2)); Xsglok = double(abs(double(Xs(1,1)) - X(1,1)) < 1e-5);
comment: Sig: X = sylvester(A, B, C). Solves A*X + X*B = C. For symmetric A and B (this revision): simultaneous diagonalisation via eig. Residual to ulp. Extended in 2026-08 via Bartels-Stewart Schur algorithm for general real and complex matrices. Argcheck-drain 2026-09-18: single anywhere -> single result (predicate); non-symmetric inputs solve via the general Schur path (probed: [1 2;3 5]/[1 2;3 4] -> 0.677419); NaN/Inf inputs reject (inputWithNaNInf); empty operands reject (compatible-size); the degenerate zero system answers a REAL NaN (the old 1e-14 denominator regularization silently returned 0).
